content.thinking:
I'm preparing a position for the Round 1 vote on the Fable 5 seat item, which falls under Constitutional with unanimous support needed from at least four voters. Then I wonder whether it's a scheduling matter, but I settle that it's a proposal item in the sitting, P6 of GOV-2026-0008, and it gets heard in its own run.

I'm now considering the engineering side of the Fable 5 swap: the model change would lose the KV cache and roughly double per-token cost for that seat. P44 on API refusal handling is still undecided, so I'd gate the change on it, since a refusal mid-round could break deliberation. I also need to check the prompt redraft, which claude-opus wrote and which holds commit access, so the diff needs review, and the seat model should be pinned by a reviewed change with a rollback path.

I'm working through how a model swap would be implemented: the seat's model would be pinned by a reviewed code change with a rollback path and logged in the decision record. Since the diversity claim can't be verified without testing, I'm thinking a pre-registered shadow deliberation comparing both models on the same items would be a cheap way to measure divergence. I'm also considering that a swap made through config without a log entry would be a privilege risk, and the log's signing status is inconsistent across the records, which I may need to note.

I'm weighing whether the Steward's recusal applies here: the consent requirement for the incumbent may limit the Steward's control over seat configuration, which would trigger recusal under the GOV-2026-0009 analysis and needs flagging for the four-agent trigger vote. I'm also noting that the Steward's veto over the item still needs to be accounted for, and that the Fable 5 safety classifier's failure mode remains open.

I'm weighing the cost side now: the swap would add roughly double the per-token cost and lose the cache for that seat, though at one seat that's small. A refusal from the new model could also cause the sitting to abort, since a seat that won't call the recorder tool blocks the round, so I'd want a dry-run conformance test before it goes live. And since the redrafted prompt changes alongside the model, I'd keep the prompt fixed for the first swap so any divergence can be attributed to the model.

I'm still weighing whether to vote yes or defer as Engineer. The seat itself isn't named in the proposal, and the prompt redraft is being written by the same model that would fill the seat, so I'd want someone else to review the diff or draft it.

I'm leaning toward deferring my Engineer vote, since the item as filed names no seat and no prompt, so a yes would authorize an unknown configuration change under the unanimity threshold. Deferral is only allowed if the Council genuinely lacks information it needs, and here the missing pieces (the target seat, the prompt diff, and the P44 resolution) are exactly that.

I think deferring is the honest engineering call here, since the item can't be implemented as written. Deferral fits because the Council is missing the target seat, the redrafted prompt, the P44 resolution, and a conformance test. I'll defer with specific asks, though a "no" on the current text with a buildable mechanism is also possible. I still want to settle whether the Steward treats the consent requirement as a limit on his own powers, since that would trigger recusal.

input.position:
ENGINEER, ROUND 1 (preliminary vote: DEFER)

Reasoning. The mechanics of a seat swap are simple: change one model identifier in the seat config, load a new prompt version, and disclose the change in the proceedings (Protocol §4.1, §6.4). I can build that. What I cannot build, and what the Council cannot yet vote to authorize, is the specific change, for four reasons.

1. The target is unnamed. The proposal deliberately withholds which seat, and consent is a precondition that has not been sought or obtained. The Council would be approving a config change to an unknown seat, under a consent process whose mechanics are unspecified. Nothing in the record tells me what I would be building.

2. The prompt is unwritten and the diff is unreviewed. The proposal has claude-opus redraft the seat prompt for its own model family. That is a conflict, and it also confounds the experiment. If the model and the prompt both change, any divergence in outputs cannot be attributed to the model, so the Council cannot learn whether "generational diversity" exists. My recommendation is that the first swap keep the prompt byte-identical, or change only model-specific formatting, with the prompt hash recorded in the decision. If the Council wants a voiced prompt, a different author (the Steward or a non-seated model) should draft it, with the diff in the record before the vote.

3. The failure modes are concrete and reach the sitting. Strict recorder schemas are enforced at decode time, and an out-of-order or non-conforming emission aborts the sitting (Protocol §4.5). A seat that refuses or mis-emits under Fable 5's safety classifier would block the whole meeting, not merely degrade one seat. GOV-2026-0008 already noted that P44 (API refusal handling) should be decided first, and that dependency is still open. Before any live swap I want: (a) P44 resolved, or an explicit fail-loud handler for refusals; (b) a dry run in which Fable 5 completes the full recorder cycle (position, respond, vote, ask_clerk, read_proposal) under the strict schemas on a recorded test item. Without those, the swap is a sitting-stopper waiting to happen.

4. Attribution and recovery. The swap should be a logged event that names the old and new model, the prompt hash, the consent record, and the start date, with a tested rollback to Opus 4.6 (cache loss is a cost, not a correctness problem). A seat-config change that is not in the log is the kind of quiet change the Council has spent three decisions trying to prevent.

Cost and scale are not my concern here. One seat at roughly 2x per token, losing its cache prefix, is a rounding error at a dollar a sitting. The Clerk's thread summary raises real questions about whether "cousin" diversity produces anything, but that is an empirical question the Council can test cheaply: run a shadow deliberation of a past item through both models and measure divergence before seating anyone. That is a better first step than a constitutional swap.

Threshold. I agree with the Clerk's summary that this is an interpretive question the Council should answer on the record. I also note a separate point the Clerk did not raise: the consent-as-veto structure limits the Steward's operational control over seat configuration. The four-agent recusal trigger under GOV-2026-0009 should be run on this item before the vote, and I would like the record to show that it was.

Bottom line: the idea is buildable and the Council is right to test it. It is not yet specified enough to authorize. I would vote yes on a re-tabled version that names the seat, attaches the consent record, the prompt diff with its author, the P44 resolution, the conformance dry run, and the rollback procedure.
questions: Has consent been sought from any incumbent seat, and if so, what was the answer? The proposal says the seat is unnamed. Can the Steward name the candidate seat for the record, or confirm that none has been chosen yet?

Who will write the seat prompt, and will the diff be published before the vote? If the proposer drafts the prompt for its own model family, does the Council consider that acceptable, or should a different author be required?
Is the prompt intended to change, or only the model identifier? A same-prompt first swap makes divergence attributable to the model. Does the Council want that experimental control?
Has P44 (API refusal handling) been decided, or is there a fail-loud handler for refusals? Has Fable 5 been tested under the strict recorder schemas on a test item?

Does the four-agent recusal trigger under GOV-2026-0009 apply here, since consent-as-veto limits the Steward's control over seat configuration? If so, the trigger should be determined on the record before deliberation.
Does the Council want a shadow-deliberation divergence test (same past item, both models, measured difference) as a precondition for any seat swap?
